The structure of Sr2Co20O28 (reduced formula SrCo10O14) crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Cmcm (No. 119), with 50 atoms per unit cell across 6 independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies cobalt in octahedral environments, with Co–O distances ranging from 1.8886 to 2.1266 Å, while strontium adopts a close-packed-like 12-coordinate O environment. The octahedra share edges, and Co–Sr polyhedra show corner- and face-sharing, forming a three-dimensional periodic connectivity network.
